reason: Idle project execution workers polled claim_next every 100 ms per lane; each empty claim was a fenced write transaction (~15 statements incl. a no-op row-lock UPDATE) and the handoff watcher opened another fenced transaction every second. The fix adds a lock-free RuntimeCoordination.dispatch_snapshot that shares claim_next's hold and lane-head rules, a per-worker probe that wakes per-lane consumers (0.1 s while a lane, a chat turn or a recent delivery is active; 0.5 s idle), 30 s safety claims and ticks, fail-open probe failure handling, handoff ticks only while a source handoff applies, and cancellation-safe waits. Selected suites cover the worker lifecycle and loops, claim/snapshot equivalence, the coordination fence, the handoff agent contract, durable delivery, and the diagnostic boundary that fakes the coordinator.
exclusions: Process-level suites (test_execution_worker_process, test_runtime_continuity_acceptance, chat resume/acceptance, memory control, restart recovery) need a pidfd-capable interpreter and a production UI build; locally all 69 of those that fail did so identically on pristine main with and without this patch (no new failures). No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. PostgreSQL variants run where NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set. Staging before/after evidence (idle CPU 3.24 -> 0.75 cores, 601 -> 190 DB transactions/s for 16 idle workers; chat-start and mid-turn Stop pickup medians 4.27 -> 1.21 s and 2.47 -> 0.84 s) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI.
